hints: Resolve all three forces into horizontal and vertical components.
Calculate the magnitude using $R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}$ and the angle $\alpha$ using $\tan\alpha = \frac{X}{Y}$.
walkthrough:
State the principle of vector resolution for coplanar forces:
The components of the resultant $\mathbf{R} = (X, Y)$ are the sums of the respective components of each individual force:
$$X = \sum F_x, \quad Y = \sum F_y$$

Calculate the horizontal component $X$:
- The $60\text{ N}$ force acts purely along the positive horizontal axis: $+60\text{ N}$.
- The $50\text{ N}$ force is directed at $20^\circ$ above the positive horizontal axis: $+50\cos 20^\circ$.
- The $100\text{ N}$ force is directed at $30^\circ$ to the left of the positive vertical axis, giving a negative horizontal component: $-100\sin 30^\circ$.
$$X = 60 + 50\cos 20^\circ - 100\sin 30^\circ$$
$$50\cos 20^\circ \approx 50 \times 0.939693 = 46.9846$$
$$100\sin 30^\circ = 100 \times 0.5 = 50$$
$$X = 60 + 46.9846 - 50 = 56.9846\text{ N}$$

Calculate the vertical component $Y$:
- The $60\text{ N}$ force has zero vertical component.
- The $50\text{ N}$ force has a downward vertical component: $-50\sin 20^\circ$.
- The $100\text{ N}$ force has an upward vertical component: $+100\cos 30^\circ$.
$$Y = 100\cos 30^\circ - 50\sin 20^\circ$$
$$100\cos 30^\circ \approx 100 \times 0.866025 = 86.6025$$
$$50\sin 20^\circ \approx 50 \times 0.342020 = 17.1010$$
$$Y = 86.6025 - 17.1010 = 69.5015\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force using Pythagoras' theorem:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{56.9846^2 + 69.5015^2}$$
$$56.9846^2 \approx 3247.25, \quad 69.5015^2 \approx 4830.46$$
$$R = \sqrt{3247.25 + 4830.46} = \sqrt{8077.71} \approx 89.876\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $R = 89.9\text{ N}$.

Calculate the direction angle $\alpha$ (measured from the vertical axis as shown in the diagram):
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{X}{Y} = \frac{56.9846}{69.5015} \approx 0.819905$$
$$\alpha = \arctan(0.819905) \approx 39.348^\circ$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $\alpha = 39.3^\circ$.
